text:
William Carrier is a fourth-liner on paper and a problem for opponents in practice. Carolina takes about 62% of the expected goals and 61% of the shot attempts when he's on the ice at five on five, and he's thrown 62 hits in 22 games on 13 minutes a night. Against Montreal on Thursday, Cory Lavalette of North State Journal saw a big hit on Kaiden Guhle and one shift good enough to compare him, tongue in cheek, to Guy Lafleur.

The one thing missing is the finish. He has 1 goal on 5.2 expected, shooting under 3%, and our numbers flag him as due: he keeps getting the looks, and goals tend to follow chances. His 11 assists are already level with last season's total.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.5 wins in 2025-26, 97th percentile at taking chances away, with the fair caveat that he plays beside strong teammates. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says his game isn't built on creating offense, which makes this season's chances all the more surprising. There was a scare before the Global Series games against Seattle, but he played both. Watch the goals: a few should come.
